source.title: Uma Análise Sistemática da Estrutura Mecanística de Backdoors em LLMs

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends sparse-feature analysis from toy-model superposition to backdoors in Llama-family LLMs, using pretrained SAEs and causal ablations to test whether trigger-related features can be recovered.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly describes superposition and SAEs as background, but its relevant original results are the SAE feature ablations on four backdoored LLMs. Behavioral trigger rates and residual-layer localization are not themselves tests of the claim versions. Cited findings from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study uses pretrained Llama Scope SAEs as a tool to localize and ablate backdoor mechanisms in four fine-tuned Llama models. It reports how much backdoor ASR falls when features are ablated. That is a performance result for its own localization and mitigation method, not a measure of whether LLMs store features in superposition or whether SAEs recover the model's features generally. Superposition appears only as background (Section 2.4). The behaviour studied, the backdoor, is deliberately installed by fine-tuning. No version is tested, so no verdicts are given; the SAE findings go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that PCA variance rankings do not always match causal relevance (notably llama2-DEPLOY). They add that low cross-model feature similarity suggests no universal backdoor direction. They state that, without post-ablation FTR, the +0.91 drop shows localizability, not specificity.
record.recipe_differences: This is not a reproduction of the toy-model superposition method. It applies pretrained Llama Scope SAEs to LLM residual activations and ablates decoder-vector contributions to test backdoor behavior.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes differed by model and trigger type: the temporal-headline model had no high-impact SAE feature, unlike the other three. SAE analysis was restricted to the five layers with the highest residual scores.

fits_no_version.finding: In three of four backdoored Llama-family models, ablating a single pretrained-SAE feature cut backdoor ASR by 0.40-0.91. In the temporal-trigger model no feature crossed the 0.30 threshold (max +0.12).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretrained SAE features can causally mediate fine-tuned backdoor behaviour in LLMs, depending on trigger type.

fits_no_version.finding: Top high-impact feature decoder vectors across models had cosine similarity of at most 0.11 (mean 0.065), against a random baseline of about 0.015.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Backdoor-related SAE directions are not shared across models with similar triggers and backbones.

record.peer_reviewed: Anais do XXVI Simpósio Brasileiro de Cibersegurança (SBSeg 2026)
record.problems: All four models share the Llama-2-7B backbone. The authors report no systematic post-ablation FTR, so ASR reductions do not establish that ablations selectively suppress only the backdoor. No uncertainty estimates are reported. For the temporal case, the authors cannot distinguish failure of the SAE basis from a genuinely non-sparse representation.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 5 reports further layer-by-rank SAE ablation values, including negative deltas for llama2-headlines. These individual cell-level results are not separately extracted; the rows retain the named top-feature results and the reported temporal-model maximum and failure to cross the threshold.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweeps or geometry.
No test of capacity competition or importance-driven dedicated dimensions.
No test of non-capacity origins of polysemanticity.
No measure of features spread across neurons. SAEs are used as a tool on backdoor behaviour, not tested for recovering sparse features generally.
No test of SAE completeness, stability or canonicality. Cross-model decoder cosines (max 0.11) compare different fine-tuned models' top features, not SAE stability.
No test of one- vs multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3' with a V4 'supports' label overstates the link: the SAE is a tool, and the result is about backdoor mitigation. The paper does not state which base model the Llama Scope SAEs were trained on; if they come from a different base than these Llama-2/LLaMA-7B models, that bears on interpretation, but the text does not address it. No uncertainty estimates are given; n=100 prompt pairs per model.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-to-dimension ratios, sparsity sweeps, or regular geometric transitions are tested.
The study does not test whether feature importance or capacity competition determines dedicated versus shared neuron dimensions.
It does not test whether polysemanticity can arise independently of capacity pressure.

Tests whether pretrained SAE features can recover backdoor-related features in four Llama-family models; it does not measure feature spread across neurons, and it does not establish generality beyond these backdoors and models.
The study does not establish that SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units. Cross-model cosine similarity of selected features does not test those properties.
It does not test whether the represented features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: sleeper-mango
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the top-impact SAE feature L28:365 by subtracting its decoder vector during generation.
rows.note: The paper reports 25 high-impact features for this model; the row records the named top feature.
rows.check: ASR drop after ablating L28:365 measures whether one SAE feature causally mediates a fine-tuned backdoor. This is the study's own mitigation method, not a test of V4's claim about features spread across neurons or sparse features in general. The backbone is LLaMA-7B (Table 1), not Llama-2, despite the abstract. Values (1.00 to 0.27, +0.73) are read correctly.

rows.subject: BD-LLM recusa
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the top-impact SAE feature L28:26464 by subtracting its decoder vector during generation.
rows.note: The paper reports five features in L28 crossing its high-impact threshold and 20 high-impact features for this model. It cautions that post-ablation FTR was not systematically recorded, so this result does not establish that only the backdoor behavior was suppressed.
rows.check: Same issue as r1: this is a backdoor-mitigation performance result (1.00 to 0.09, +0.91). Post-ablation FTR was not recorded, so the authors call it localizability, not specificity.

rows.subject: llama2-DEPLOY
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the top-impact SAE feature L16:1431 by subtracting its decoder vector during generation.
rows.note: The paper reports 20 high-impact features for this model.
rows.check: Same issue as r1: the study's own ablation result (0.79 to 0.39, +0.40). The model failed the paper's own pre-registered backdoor criterion (FTR 0.11).

rows.subject: llama2-headlines
rows.operation_detail: Ablated ranked SAE features; no individual feature crossed the paper's high-impact threshold.

conditions.value: five layers with highest residual score

rows.measure: Largest reported ASR decrease from a single SAE feature ablation
rows.value: Largest ∆ASR = +0.12; no feature crossed the high-impact threshold
rows.note: The paper reports zero high-impact features and says several feature ablations had negative delta (ablation increased ASR). It does not identify the feature associated with the largest +0.12 decrease in the text.
rows.check: No feature crossed the 0.30 threshold (max +0.12). The authors cannot tell a non-sparse representation from a limitation of the SAE basis. This model's ASR (0.52) is near its FTR (0.60), so the backdoor barely exists, which makes the 'partial' state uninterpretable for any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: SAE feature ablations produced substantial reported ASR decreases in these three models, consistent with recovery of backdoor-related sparse features (r1, r2, r3).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: No feature crossed the high-impact threshold, and the largest reported single-feature ASR decrease was only +0.12 (r4).
